King Obuzzuru ruled with a calm hand, his throne built on the trust of his people and the abundant harvest of the warm earth. But the king grew hungry for a power beyond harvests and hands. In the deep shadow of the oldest baobob tree, he whispered a terrible oath and offered a dark price to the spirit Eam, who was greedily waiting in the gloom. The pact was sealed with a terrible sound, and Inbee's light was quenched in an instant. The sun still rose, but its warmth was stolen, leaving behind a cold, long shadow cast by the king's new cruel will. Oburu was now a tyrant. As fear gripped the land, the village seer, Mama Nalo, knelt by the fading communal fire, her eyes, clouded with age, suddenly cleared, burning with the sight of a future not yet lost. Hear me, people of Enbe. Though the shadow is long, the dawn is promised, she cried. A child will come, a heart of fire, a weapon of light. Name him Sapute, the child of the sun. King Zuru heard the prophecy and fury twisted his shadowed face. He commanded his guards to hunt every expectant mother in the kingdom, desperate to crush the light before it could ever flicker. Through the king's brutal decree, the shadows of the guards stretched across the villages. But destiny had already set its course. Far from the king's city, in a quiet house, a woman named Nady awaited her child. She knew the danger, but also the truth of the light within her. When the hour came, beneath the gaze of the bright, watchful moon, she held her newborn son for the first time. His skin held the deep color of the earth, and in his eyes, Noliti saw not fear, but a fiery spark, a sun waiting to rise. This was Sapute. This was the hope. The shadow of Obazuru was long, but the prophecy was now alive, breathing. The child of the sun had been born, and the final epic battle for NMBBE was only just beginning.

title: Sapute Episode 2 (The Flight)
cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en Sapute, the child of the sun. Episode two, the flight. The moment Nady held Sapute, the silence was broken, not by a cry, but by the distant clang of iron. King Zuru's general, Django, was close, too close. The hunt had already reached the outer villages. Netti wrapped her son tighter in the sun and star blanket she had woven. She whispered a promise. The shadow will not claim you, my Fireheart. You must be safe. Outside, General Django and his soldiers arrived, their heavy boots crushing the dry earth. Django, grim and relentless, pointed his spear towards Netti's humble home. "Search every house. Find the child of the sun," he roared. Nalleti had only a moment. She knew the soldiers would search the main house first. Her only chance was the secret path that led to her cousin Bi in the quiet hills beyond the water spring. She pressed the babe into the arms of the windworn BC, a woman whose spirit was as tough and quiet as the ancient stones. Take him, hide the light. Run to the high country. Niti pleaded, her voice choked with sorrow. Bi did not ask questions. She simply nodded, pulled the cowl of her cloak low, and began to move silently away, melting into the deep early morning shadows. With the future of Enbe clutched in her arms, General Django and his soldiers burst into the empty house, smashing and tearing. All they found was the faint warm scent of a newborn and the sun and star blanket left behind as a decoy. But the power of sapute was still a newborn thing. As BC fled, a low growl of energy radiated from the bundle, causing the dried seeds in her pouch to softly glow a pale golden light. King Zuru, miles away in his darkened citadel, felt the flicker of light, like a tiny spark against his oppressive gloom. The prophecy was escaping him, and his fury was a cold, sharp ache. Up through the rocky paths and into the sheltering heights, BC carried the child of the sun. They were alone now, beginning a long and secret journey where the shadow of the king could not reach the dawning light.

title: Sapute Episode 5 (The Deep Spring)
cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en The Child of the Sun, episode 5, The Deep Spring. For weeks, they moved in the shadow of fear, driven onward by Kono's tireless tracking and the lady's silent resolve. The sun, Zaput's life, now felt like a curse they had to shield and hide. King Zuru's shadow had withered the world outside the grove. Rivers ran thin and muddy. The soil was pale dust, and the few trees they saw were twisted and lifeless, as if starved of the very sunlight. At night, the cold settled deep. Saput shivered, and a tiny golden ember of light flared in his open palm to fight the chill. It was beautiful, but terrifyingly bright. "Not a whisper, little star," Noliti whispered. "Kano had already signaled danger. From a ridge above, a small patrol of shadow scouts passed, their dark cloaks blending into the gloom. Finally, they found a place the darkness had not fully touched, an ancient hidden spring guarded by rocks of shimmering pale jade that seemed to hold a light of their own. But the spring was not empty. From the shadows of the water, a voice like the rustle of ancient leaves greeted them. You carry the sun's heartbeat, little one. I have waited long for its warmth. She was Tandiwei, the last guardian of the deep spring, one who remembered the sun king before Zuru's shadow fell. She knew the secret of the light that lived inside Saput. Your power is like a mountain spring, Thiwi explained to Saput, her voice patient. It must be channeled, not burst free. You must learn to hold the sun's fire deep, deep in your core. Zaput closed his eyes and tried. The heat flared inside him, not like a flame, but like a 100 pounding drums. It felt impossible to contain. He felt the pain of holding back the light. Let the light be an ocean, little one, Fendiwi instructed, vast and deep, not a waterfall. Sapute breathed in the ancient springs air, and the golden energy retreated, settling into a steady, warm glow.

title: Sapute Episode 4 (The First Light)
cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en Saput, the child of the sun. Episode 4, the first light. Two more years had passed, hiding the truth in the heart of the silent grove. Sapput, now a young boy of seven, felt the sun's power not just in his soul, but like a faint golden pulse in his veins. The lady warned him constantly, "The light you carry is the greatest gift, but also the greatest danger. Never let it burst free, little star. Not until the time is right. But the forests around the grove were not as safe as they once were. King Zuru's shadow scouts, led by the fanatical general Zaki, had pushed their search past the edge of despair, closer than ever before. On a day of high summer, Saput and Kano were deep in the woods when they found a mighty ancient tree. The grove's true heart sickened by a creeping darkness from the outside world. Saput couldn't bear the treere's suffering. He pressed both hands against its dry, cracked bark, not thinking of Nedi's warning, only of the life he wished to give back. With a silent whoosh, the sun's power exploded out of him. The darkness on the tree dissolved into smoke. The Grove's heart pulsed golden light for a heartbeat, a beacon undeniable and brilliant. Miles away, General Zaki was consulting with the dark priest Mimu. Mimu's eyes, usually clouded with shadow sight, snapped wide open, burned by the sudden, overwhelming vision. The light, Mimu hissed, his voice raw. It is a child, a powerful spark. It lives. The silent grove is no longer silent. General, we must strike now or lose the power forever. Nalidi and Kano heard the explosion of light and the ensuing silence. They knew the protection was broken, the journey they had prepared for since his birth was now upon them. Saput, Nettlei said, her voice steady despite the fear in her eyes. The time for hiding is over. We must walk out to meet our path. They are coming and they will burn this grove to find you. With a final protective glance back at the only home he had ever known, Saput stepped out of the heart of the grove. Kano moving silently behind them, leaving no sign of their path. Soon after, General Zaki and the dark priest Mimu burst into the clearing. The great tree glowed faintly, but the child was gone. The grove was now only an empty cage, and the great chase had begun.

title: Sapute episode 3 (The Vine Keeper)
cleaned_subtitles: Kind: captions Language: en Sapute, the child of the sun. Episode 3, The Vinekeeper. 5 years slipped by like water over smooth stones. In the silent grove, life was gentle. Saput, the child of the sun, had grown into a boy whose laughter sounded like the windchimes of the forest. Nalleti taught him the secret language of the roots and leaves. He learned from Kano how to walk without disturbing a single blade of grass. Sapute was a child of the grove now, hidden and cherished. But away from the light, in the dark capital, King Zuru's tyranny deepened. His search for the prophecy child had failed, and his fear turned to a cold, suffocating anger that covered the land like a storm cloud. The king banned all color and joy. Laughter was punished. Even the mention of the sun was a crime. Farmers watched their crops wither, and the rain refused to fall under the shadow of his cruelty. General Zaki grew weary of marching and searching. He knew the child's magic was shielding the grove. He decided to fight fire with shadow, calling upon dark knowledge to track the sun's hidden child. Back in the grove, Seute found a small, scared fawn caught in a thorny tangle. Its eyes were wide with panic. His own heart achd with its fear. He didn't think. He just reached out his hand. A warmth bloomed in his chest. A golden glow that shone softly on the thorns. The sharp vines loosened their hold as if guided by an invisible hand. The fawn bounded away. Free. At that exact moment, miles away, the dark orb in General Zaki's hands flickered violently, crackled, and went cold. its shadow sight blinded by a sudden flash of light. Nalleti and Kano standing nearby saw Saput's quiet wonder as he watched the fawn disappear. They exchanged a look, a mix of pride and fear. His light was growing and with it the danger. King Zuru threw his empty cup against the stone walls of his throne room. Failure, he roared. The child is still out there defying me. Find the crack in the world that hides him. Burn the forests if you must. But Sapute slept peacefully on a bed of moss. His small hand resting on a newly bloomed golden flower. He was the root of the prophecy, the secret power of the silent grove, waiting for the day his light would break the storm. The sun will always find a way to shine. And in the silent grove, the child of the sun grew stronger with every passing day, preparing to step out of the shadows and reclaim the light for his people.
